title: How a Vector Grows
prompt: Built with g++ (libstdc++). Which capacities does this print?
explanation:
libstdc++ doubles the capacity whenever the vector is full. Each reallocation allocates a new buffer, moves every element across, and frees the old one.

Why doubling: copying n elements is expensive, but it happens only after n cheap pushes. Total work for n pushes is about n + n/2 + n/4 + … < 2n, so `push_back` is **amortized O(1)**. Growing by a constant amount (say +10) instead would make n pushes cost O(n²).

The growth factor isn't fixed by the standard: MSVC grows by 1.5×, which would give the last option. If you know the final size, `v.reserve(n)` avoids all the reallocations.
try_this: Add `v.reserve(20);` before the loop. How many lines of output now?
